appearance_facts.fact: Title: 'Incidence of Condition A in US States'.
Map of the United States with states colored by incidence level of Condition A.
Color scale legend on the right: 'Low' (dark red) to 'High' (light yellow), with labeled tick values: 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100.
States are labeled with two-letter postal abbreviations (e.g., WA, TX, CO).
Color gradient: Light yellow indicates high incidence (near 100), dark red indicates low incidence (near 0).

States with no data or not applicable are shaded gray (e.g., AK, HI, MT, ND, SD, WY, UT, NV, AZ, CA, MS, AL, AR, TN, KY, WV, VA, SC, NC, GA, FL, LA, OK, NM, KS, MO, IL, IN, OH, MI, WI, MN, IA, NE, OR, ID, MT, ND, SD, WY, UT, NV, AZ, CA, MS, AL, AR, TN, KY, WV, VA, SC, NC, GA, FL, LA, OK, NM, KS, MO, IL, IN, OH, MI, WI, MN, IA, NE, OR, ID).
Texas (TX) is colored light yellow, indicating high incidence.
Washington (WA) is colored dark red, indicating low incidence.

printed_facts.fact: The color scale legend ranges from 0 (Low) to 100 (High).
Texas (TX) is shaded light yellow, corresponding to a value near 100 on the scale.
Washington (WA) is shaded dark red, corresponding to a value near 0 on the scale.
Colorado (CO) is shaded dark red, corresponding to a value near 0 on the scale.

public_definitions: The task requires reviewing the state incidence dashboard to identify the jurisdiction with the highest incidence of Condition A for follow-up routing.
The dashboard is the evidence source for routing decisions.
The options provided are to open the incidence profile for Texas (TX), Washington (WA), or Colorado (CO).
